accepted.s: With reference to limits applicable to Foreign Portfolio Investors in government securities, which one of the following is correct?
o: 2% of outstanding Central Government securities and 6% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
10% of outstanding Central Government securities and 5% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 6% of outstanding State Government securities under the General Route
accepted.x: Under the General Route, the overall FPI limit is 6% of outstanding Central Government securities and 2% of outstanding State Government securities. Security-wise and short-term limits have been removed.
accepted.tq: Use the paired percentages and avoid reversing the Central and State figures.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) for foreign investment in government securities:
1. FAR securities are not subject to investment limits.
2. New 15-year, 30-year and 40-year Government securities are covered under FAR.
3. Sovereign green bonds are covered under FAR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. FAR removes investment limits for specified securities, including new 15-year, 30-year and 40-year Government securities and sovereign green bonds.
accepted.tq: Check whether all listed categories fall within the stated no-limit route.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the distinction between FDI and FPI under the threshold prescribed for investment in a listed company?
o: An equity holding of 25% or more is treated as FDI, while a holding below 25% is treated as FPI
All equity investment in a listed company is treated as FDI, irrespective of the percentage held
An equity holding below 10% is treated as FDI, while a holding of 10% or more is treated as FPI
An equity holding of 10% or more is treated as FDI, while a holding below 10% is treated as FPI
accepted.x: Under the relevant FEMA threshold, an equity holding of 10% or more in a listed company is classified as FDI, while a holding below 10% is classified as FPI. Any stake in an unlisted company is treated as FDI.
accepted.tq: Separate the 10% listed-company threshold from the special rule for unlisted companies.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Foreign Portfolio Investment in India is correct?
o: FPI was opened to India in 2000 and is regulated exclusively by the Ministry of Finance
FPI was opened to India in 1991 and is regulated exclusively by the RBI under FEMA
FPI was opened to India in 1992 and is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, along with the RBI
FPI was opened to India in 2019 and is regulated exclusively by SEBI without any role for the RBI
accepted.x: Foreign Portfolio Investment was opened to India in 1992. It is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, with the RBI also having a regulatory role.
accepted.tq: Combine the opening year with the two relevant regulators rather than selecting an exclusive regulator.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about recent FPI flows and their determinants:
1. FPI flows are influenced significantly by US Federal Reserve interest rates and global risk appetite.
2. A flight to safety may lead to FPI outflows from India.
3. Domestic fundamentals are identified as the sole determinant of FPI flows.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. FPI flows are strongly affected by US interest rates and global risk sentiment, and a flight to safety can cause outflows; domestic fundamentals are not the sole determinant.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word 'sole' when the material identifies multiple external drivers.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported FPI equity outflow by May 2026 and the outflow during May alone?
o: Over ₹1 lakh crore by May 2026 and ₹12,829 crore in May alone
Over ₹2 lakh crore by May 2026 and ₹24,829 crore in May alone
Over ₹3 lakh crore by May 2026 and ₹24,829 crore in May alone
About ₹2 lakh crore by May 2026 and ₹42,829 crore in May alone
accepted.x: FPIs had withdrawn over ₹2 lakh crore from equities by May 2026, including ₹24,829 crore during May alone. These outflows were identified as a key cause of rupee weakness.
accepted.tq: Match the cumulative figure with the monthly component without confusing their scales.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to FPI flows in FY 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The reported overall FPI outflow was about ₹2.2 lakh crore.
2. Net FPI outflow in March 2026 was reported at 13.6 billion US dollars.
3. FPI outflows pushed the rupee beyond ₹96 per US dollar in May 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the FY26 outflow was about ₹2.2 lakh crore, March 2026 recorded a net outflow of $13.6 billion, and the rupee crossed ₹96 per US dollar in May 2026 amid the outflows.
accepted.tq: Retain the different units—rupees, dollars and exchange rate—while checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index is expected to have which of the following effects?
o: It shifts all FPI investment from equities to State securities
It fixes the exchange rate of the rupee at a predetermined level
It attracts passive bond inflows through a target weight of 10%
It prohibits foreign investment in Indian government securities
accepted.x: India's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index, with a target weight of 10%, is expected to draw passive bond inflows.
accepted.tq: Link index inclusion with the passive investment flows it mechanically generates.
accepted.sec: FPI flows - limits, drivers, trend  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding regional and bilateral trade agreements:
List-I (Agreement)
a. SAPTA
b. SAFTA
c. India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement
d. India-UAE CEPA
List-II (Year)
i. 2022
ii. 2009
iii. 1993
iv. 2004
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i
a–iv, b–iii, c–ii, d–i
a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
a–ii, b–iv, c–iii, d–i
accepted.x: SAPTA was signed in 1993, SAFTA in 2004, the India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement in 2009, and the India-UAE CEPA in 2022.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure agreement-year pairs and eliminate codes that disturb them.
accepted.sec: FTAs and CEPAs - partner and year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the agreement with its date or status?
o: India-Australia ECTA — in force from December 2022
India-EFTA TEPA — signed in December 2025
India-UK CETA — signed in March 2024
India-Oman CEPA — in force from 1 January 2006
accepted.x: The India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement came into force in December 2022. The India-EFTA TEPA was signed in March 2024, the India-UK CETA in July 2025, and India-Oman CEPA dates to December 2025.
accepted.tq: Use the agreement dates as anchors and identify the incorrectly paired alternatives.
accepted.sec: FTAs and CEPAs - partner and year  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent trade agreements of India:
1. The India-EFTA TEPA was signed in March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025.
2. The India-EFTA arrangement includes a pledge of 100 billion US dollars in investment and one million jobs.
3. The India-UK CETA provides duty-free access for 99% of Indian exports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The EFTA TEPA has the stated dates and investment-employment pledge, while the India-UK CETA provides duty-free access for 99% of Indian exports.
accepted.tq: Test the date, numerical pledge and coverage percentage separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: FTAs and CEPAs - partner and year  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about India's recent agreements with the United Kingdom and the European Union is correct?
o: The India-EU FTA covers less than 500 million people and eliminates tariffs on all goods
The India-UK CETA was signed on 27 January 2026 and is awaiting ratification
The India-UK CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026
The India-EU FTA entered into force on 1 October 2025 after being signed in March 2024
accepted.x: The India-UK CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026. The India-EU FTA negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026, but ratification was still pending; it covers about 2 billion people and cuts tariffs on more than 90% of goods.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a concluded and ratified agreement from one whose negotiations have concluded but ratification is pending.
accepted.sec: FTAs and CEPAs - partner and year  [other exams]

accepted.s: In December 2025, India signed or concluded agreements with which of the following combinations of partners?
o: China and South Korea
Oman and New Zealand
Australia and Switzerland
The United Kingdom and the European Union
accepted.x: The India-Oman CEPA and the India-New Zealand FTA are associated with December 2025. The Australia agreement dates to 2022, while the EFTA and UK agreements have different dates.
accepted.tq: Use the year-partner combination rather than matching a partner with a better-known but different agreement.
accepted.sec: FTAs and CEPAs - partner and year  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) consists of ASEAN-10 and which of the following countries?
o: India, China, Japan, Russia and Australia
China, India, South Korea, Canada and New Zealand
Japan, the United States, Australia, India and Indonesia
China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand
accepted.x: RCEP comprises the ten ASEAN countries along with China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand. India is not a member because it opted out in 2019.
accepted.tq: Separate the ASEAN core from the five named partner countries and exclude India.
accepted.sec: RCEP and ASEAN partners - India's withdrawal  [other exams]

accepted.s: Why did India opt out of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership in 2019?
o: A prohibition on all Indian exports to Australia and New Zealand
The requirement that India withdraw from the World Trade Organization
Concerns regarding China's market dominance, a widening trade deficit with China, and risks to farm, dairy and small industries
The absence of any ASEAN country from the proposed partnership
accepted.x: India withdrew over concerns about China's market dominance, the rise in its trade deficit with China, and possible adverse effects on agriculture, dairy and small industries. The deficit rose from $53.5 billion in 2018–19 to $99.2 billion in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines the stated market, trade-deficit and domestic-industry concerns.
accepted.sec: RCEP and ASEAN partners - India's withdrawal  [other exams]

accepted.s: The trade deficit between India and China mentioned in the context of India's RCEP withdrawal increased from approximately what amount in 2018–19 to what amount in 2024–25?
o: $35.5 billion to $79.2 billion
$63.5 billion to $109.2 billion
$53.5 billion to $99.2 billion
$53.5 billion to $89.2 billion
accepted.x: The India-China trade deficit increased from $53.5 billion in 2018–19 to $99.2 billion in 2024–25, strengthening concerns associated with joining RCEP.
accepted.tq: Read the two-year sequence carefully and avoid changing either the starting or ending figure.
accepted.sec: RCEP and ASEAN partners - India's withdrawal  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to Press Note 3 of 2020, consider the following statements:
1. It required Government approval for FDI from countries sharing a land border with India.
2. It was issued in April 2020.
3. It was introduced partly to prevent opportunistic takeovers during the COVID-19 period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Press Note 3, issued in April 2020, required Government approval for FDI from land-border countries and sought to prevent opportunistic takeovers during the COVID-19 period.
accepted.tq: Check the policy requirement, issue date and stated purpose as separate components.
accepted.sec: Press Note 3 - FDI from land-border countries

accepted.s: Which of the following countries was included among the countries sharing a land border with India whose FDI was covered by Press Note 3 of 2020?
o: Maldives
Bhutan
Sri Lanka
Thailand
accepted.x: The countries listed were China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan. Sri Lanka, Thailand and Maldives were not part of that stated land-border list.
accepted.tq: Test membership in the named list rather than relying on regional proximity.
accepted.sec: Press Note 3 - FDI from land-border countries

accepted.s: Under the March 2026 amendment to Press Note 3, which one of the following entities may invest through the automatic route from 1 May 2026, subject to the stated condition?
o: Any company registered in China with up to 10% Chinese ownership
A foreign firm with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership of up to 10%, provided it is not registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country
Any entity registered in a land-border country without Government approval
A company registered in Hong Kong with beneficial ownership exceeding 10%
accepted.x: From 1 May 2026, foreign firms with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership up to 10% may use the automatic route, but entities registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country remain excluded. Beneficial ownership is defined under the PML Rules, 2005.
accepted.tq: Separate beneficial ownership from place of registration and apply both conditions together.
accepted.sec: Press Note 3 - FDI from land-border countries

accepted.s: As of August 2026, how many projects involving the amended Press Note 3 route had been received, and what was their reported value?
o: 29 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore
39 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore
29 projects worth ₹5,895.65 crore
19 projects worth ₹3,895.65 crore
accepted.x: By August 2026, 29 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore had been received under the amended framework.
accepted.tq: Match the project count with its exact monetary value instead of accepting a near figure.
accepted.sec: Press Note 3 - FDI from land-border countries

accepted.s: After the abolition of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB), where are Government-route FDI applications submitted?
o: Only to the Reserve Bank of India through the ECB Portal
To the concerned ministries or departments through the FIF Portal run by DPIIT
Directly to the Ministry of Finance without any online portal
To the abolished FIPB through the Foreign Investment Facilitation Committee
accepted.x: FIPB was abolished in June 2017. Government-route applications are submitted to the concerned ministries or departments through the FIF Portal operated by DPIIT.
accepted.tq: Use the successor institution and the correct application channel rather than the abolished body.
accepted.sec: Policy bodies and regulators - FIPB successor, DPIIT, FEMA, ECB  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT):
1. It is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
2. It is the nodal department for FDI policy and FDI data.
3. Since August 2022, its FIF Portal has formed part of the National Single Window System.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. DPIIT is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, handles the nodal role for FDI policy and data, and its FIF Portal has been part of the National Single Window System since August 2022.
accepted.tq: Verify the department, its nodal responsibility and the portal integration date separately.
accepted.sec: Policy bodies and regulators - FIPB successor, DPIIT, FEMA, ECB  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship among FEMA, FERA and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs)?
o: FERA, 1973 replaced FEMA, 1999, and ECBs are regulated by SEBI under FERA
FEMA, 1999 regulates only domestic currency transactions, while ECBs are outside its scope
ECBs are regulated by the Ministry of Commerce under the Consolidated FDI Policy and not under FEMA
FEMA, 1999 replaced FERA, 1973, and ECBs are regulated by the RBI under FEMA
accepted.x: The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973. External Commercial Borrowings are regulated by the RBI under FEMA.
accepted.tq: Keep the replacement sequence and the regulator’s role distinct from the earlier law.
accepted.sec: Policy bodies and regulators - FIPB successor, DPIIT, FEMA, ECB  [GROUP-II]
